unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Nahman asks his father, R. Mordechai of Lechovich, whether the famous tzaddikim of the generation can be among the hidden 36, and the father answers in Yiddish. It is a minimal question-and-answer exchange within a section on the 36 righteous.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a series on the 36 tzaddikim; the next division begins another account on the same theme (the Rebbe of Kotzk on the Rebbe of Gostynin).

stories.start_quote: וזה של"ו צדיקים שישנם בכל דוד
stories.end_quote: ראה כמה גדלה קדושתם ז״ל זי״ע ועכי״א
stories.summary_en: R. Nahman asks his father R. Mordechai of Lechovich how the famous tzaddikim of their generation can be among the 36 if the 36 are hidden. The father replies in Yiddish that it would be a fine thing if they were no more than what people see of them, implying that their true holiness is itself hidden.

quotes: של"ו צדיקים שישנם בכל דוד קוראין אותם העולם נסתרין
tags.why: The 36 hidden righteous are the subject of the exchange.
A father and son, both tzaddikim, conduct the exchange.
The father's answer understates what is visible of the tzaddikim.

quotes: הצדיקים שבדורינו המפורסמים חיים מל״ו צדיקים
tags.why: The exchange concerns the hidden stature of the generation's tzaddikim.
The narrator's closing line praises their holiness.
